page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.medium is a compute-optimized, eighth-generation instance powered by a single dedicated 2.8 GHz AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical core. It features 2.0 GB of RAM, giving it a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio typical of compute-focused hardware profiles. The instance incorporates 59 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage, baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. CPU cache specifications include 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions enabled.

Benchmark data reflects a specialized single-core profile. In single-core execution, the Graviton processor achieves solid results in targeted tasks, such as single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.06 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 30.06 GB/sec. However, because the instance relies on a single vCPU, total multi-core execution throughput is constrained, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 986.06 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 1692.09. Uncached memory write bandwidth reaches 11.92 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 2.29 GB/sec and Redis SET operations deliver 2.38 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, c8gd.medium offers an entry-level point into the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 ecosystem paired with high-speed local NVMe instance storage. This combination eliminates network-attached storage latency for transient data without necessitating large instance sizing. Tradeoffs stem from memory capacity limitations of 2.0 GB and single-thread execution ceilings, making it unsuitable for multi-threaded batch processing or memory-intensive databases. It fits small-scale microservices, light web serving, local NVMe cache-heavy utility tasks, single-threaded processing pipelines, and lightweight edge API gateways.

Equipped with a single dedicated physical core and 2.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio alongside 59 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage. Built on the AWS Nitro system, it delivers 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Single-core benchmark performance shows high efficiency in decompression tasks, such as bzip3 decompression at 14.06 GB/sec, alongside average single-threaded compression performance. Due to its single vCPU configuration, overall multi-core throughput and total memory bandwidth remain constrained. The presence of direct-attached NVMe storage provides qualitative cost efficiency for transient data workloads requiring fast local disk access. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch tasks, small web utilities, and local caching applications.
